review_items.rationale:
Reviewed artifact c9313106842f45babd450ec50a1ad648 version 2, including its fixed root launcher and embedded internal/raft helper, against C-forwarded-context version 1 and BD-forwarded-context version 1. The package repair changed only how the same driver is compiled/invoked; the root launcher forwards stdout/stderr and propagates failure. Execution c062d2922ab74798a0e7788936085d88 completed with exit 0 and no changed target files. The raw log, not Go test success, supplies the measured comparison. Both fresh-network scenarios established term 2, commit/applied index 4 and three voters after actual bootstrap, Tick election, voting, replication and no-op commitment. The adapter saves entries/state before delivering messages, commits updates, consumes only initialized membership and no-op entries sequentially, and notifies actual consumed applied progress. Applying bootstrap members again is idempotent in the already bootstrapped Peer; no protocol state, handler or generated message is modified. In-memory TestLogDB substitutes crash-free storage, and no crash or real disk persistence is claimed. One follower request per origin per scenario is issued through Peer.ReadIndex; actual follower forwarding creates the leader queue entries and actual heartbeat producers/responses form confirmation. Later probes are delivered before held earlier probes, and every generated message is eventually drained. M-transport-order explicitly permits out-of-order message batch delivery, so this is within the implementation transport contract rather than an assumed relaxation. The schedule preserves the investigated overlap; it does not serialize it away.

The requirement is supported independently of the suspect sender: M-read-prefix-test checks original ctx/from on each prefix-released status even when index rises, M-read-receiver-test checks transfer of received context to readiness, and the client admission/consumer binds the operation to an exact SystemCtx. The claim concerns a completed response route retaining that key, not unconditional admission-to-success progress. The monitor chooses read_admitted explicitly and correlates by scenario plus origin, which is unique because each of nodes 2 and 3 has only one read in each fresh network. Expected ctx is the original input recorded after real leader admission; observed ctx is copied from the receiving Peer Update ReadyToReads before Commit clears it. No result is suppressed by matching ctx or index. A read-only queue lookup establishes admission, not the outcome.

The retained events show serial node 2 admitted/exported 101:1001 and serial node 3 admitted/exported 202:2002. In overlap, node 2 admission at index 4 was 101:1001, then node 3 admission was 202:2002 with pending_count 2. The leader emitted ReadIndexResp to each destination with 202:2002. Node 2 then exported ReadyToRead 202:2002 at index 4, while node 3 exported its correct 202:2002. Final diagnostics show pending_count 0 and two results in each scenario after all held messages were delivered. Thus the valid violating witness is overlap/origin 2 (monitor event index 13 correlated to admission index 9); the other three comparisons match. There are no parsing errors, missing result fields or ambiguous associations. Source inspection identifies the same cause: confirm retains each s.ctx, but remote routing uses incoming m.Hint/m.HintHigh for every s, while the local branch uses s.ctx. No separate application Lookup or client timeout is observed. The exact mismatch establishes the scoped requirement violation; wider liveness/safety consequences remain excluded rather than inferred from finite draining.

Explained alternatives retained: The serial control preserves both contexts; local leader readiness uses each status context. Queue coalescing may legitimately advance earlier read indices; this checker compares only the context, not an overstrong index equality. Dropped/timed-out client operations are permitted by the API and do not themselves violate this claim. Here the decisive observation is an actually completed exported route with the wrong key.

review_items.report_answer: 在三投票节点、任期稳定且当前任期已提交的执行中，节点 2 提交上下文 101:1001，却收到并导出节点 3 的 202:2002；顺序执行对照保持了各自上下文。该证据验证的是 Peer 层响应关联错误，未证明应用读取违反线性一致性或客户端永久停滞。
limitations: This is a Peer-level response/readiness identity defect in the fixed three-full-voter, stable-term, crash-free scope; it is not an observed application read linearizability violation.
The driver does not execute pendingReadIndex client deadline handling, NodeHost request completion, application Lookup, real transport or disk crash recovery.
Only the executed overlap and serial control are measured. No statement that every concurrent read schedule fails, nor that all read paths or authority transitions are covered.
Version 1 remains a package-discovery failure before prerequisites; it supplies no property evidence.
